item.name: Codex of the Last Archivist
entries: This black, leather-like spellbook is bound in tarnished silver and sealed by an eye-shaped clasp. Its pages appear blank until touched by an attuned creature, whereupon silver script emerges across them. No reliable record identifies its maker or origin.

entries.name: Arcane Supremacy
entries: While holding the codex, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells. The codex can be used as a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Endless Archive
entries: The codex can be used as a spellbook and can contain any number of Wizard spells.
The time and gold required to copy a spell into the codex are halved.

When you finish a Long Rest, choose one Wizard spell recorded in the codex. That spell is always prepared for you until you finish your next Long Rest, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

entries.name: Forbidden Index
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks concerning spells, magical writing, curses, artifacts, or lost magic.
You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} from the codex without expending a spell slot.

entries.name: Archive the Unwritten
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 through 9, you can take a Reaction to record an echo of that spell in the codex as an Archived Spell.

Before you finish your next Long Rest, you can cast the Archived Spell once without expending a spell slot and without providing any Material components, regardless of their cost or whether they would normally be consumed. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.
Once you successfully archive a spell with this property, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Perfect Recollection
entries: When you cast a spell recorded in the codex using a spell slot, choose one of the following benefits:

items: You have Advantage on one spell attack roll made as part of the spell.
One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.
The spell ignores Resistance to one damage type it deals.

entries: You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Unbroken Formula
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.
When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Final Annotation
entries: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can choose to succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Ascendant Script Tattoo
entries: This tattoo resembles a line of arcane notation written directly into the skin. The symbols subtly rearrange themselves whenever their bearer casts a spell.

entries.name: Ascendant Casting
entries: When you cast a spell of level 1 through 8 using a spell slot, you can expend charges to treat the spell as though it were cast using a spell slot one level higher for each charge expended, to a maximum effective spell level of 9. You can expend no more than 2 charges on a single spell.

entries.name: Overflowing Spell
entries: When you use Ascendant Casting, you can expend 1 additional charge and choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Empowered.} Reroll a number of the spell's damage dice up to your Proficiency Bonus. You must use the new rolls.
{@b Extended.} If the spell has a duration of at least 1 minute and isn't Instantaneous, double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If the spell has a range of at least 10 feet, double its range. If its range is Touch, its range becomes 30 feet.
{@b Overwhelming.} One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.

entries.name: Restored Script
entries: The tattoo regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Mantle of the Unbroken Spell
entries: Arcane notation drifts across this dark mantle like ink beneath water. No maker's mark has ever been found on it.

entries.name: Unbroken Concentration
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.

entries.name: Spell Refuses to Break
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can choose to succeed instead. You can use this property twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Stability
entries: When you take damage while concentrating on a spell, you can reduce the DC of the resulting Constitution saving throw by 5, to a minimum DC of 10.
You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Persistent Spell
entries: If you become Incapacitated while concentrating on a spell, your Concentration doesn't immediately end. It ends at the end of your next turn unless you are no longer Incapacitated before then.
This property can't prevent death from ending your Concentration.

item.name: Earring of the Silent Word
entries: This single black earring bears one arcane glyph that has resisted every attempt at translation. Its origin is unknown.

entries.name: Silent Casting
entries: While wearing the earring, you can cast any spell that has a Verbal component without providing that Verbal component. Any Somatic or Material components are still required.

entries.name: Unspoken Word
entries: A spell cast without its Verbal component through this item produces no spoken incantation or sound from that component. A creature can't detect the casting solely by hearing speech, though this property doesn't conceal other components, visible manifestations, or sounds produced by the spell itself.

item.name: Coin of the Open Rite
entries: This old silver coin bears an incomplete magical circle resembling an open doorway. No known mint claims its design.

entries.name: Open Rite
entries: You can cast a prepared spell of level 1 through 3 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell's normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.

Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Greater Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The circle engraved on this silver coin is nearly complete, except for a narrow break at its center.

entries.name: Greater Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 5 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.

Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. A spell recorded in a spellbook or similar source doesn't need to be prepared for you to cast it this way.
You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Grand Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The engraved circle on this coin appears complete until viewed closely, when a hairline opening becomes visible along its edge.

entries.name: Grand Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 7 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.
Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must be capable of casting spells of the chosen spell's level.

entries.name: Open Beyond Preparation
entries: You can cast an eligible spell directly from a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you even if the spell isn't prepared.

entries.name: Patient Invocation
entries: When using this coin, you can increase the additional casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour. If you do, you don't need to provide Material components that aren't consumed and have a listed cost of 1,000 GP or less.
Consumed Material components and non-consumed components worth more than 1,000 GP are still required.

item.name: Final Coin of the Open Rite
entries: No visible break exists in the circle engraved upon this coin, yet its design still gives the unmistakable impression of an open door.

entries.name: Final Open Rite
entries: You can cast a spell of level 1 through 9 as a Ritual even if the spell doesn't have the Ritual tag. The spell must be known by you, prepared by you, or recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you, and its normal casting time must be 1 minute or less.
Casting a spell this way increases its casting time by 10 minutes and doesn't expend a spell slot. You must be capable of casting spells of the chosen spell's level.

entries.name: Ninth Door
entries: An eligible spell recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source can be cast through the coin even if the spell isn't on your class's spell list. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.

entries.name: Perfect Invocation
entries: When using this coin, you can increase the additional casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour. If you do, you don't need to provide Material components with a listed cost if those components aren't consumed by the spell.
Consumed Material components are still required.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Time
entries: Instead of the normal additional casting time, you can perform the rite over 8 hours. If you do, the coin can replace consumed Material components with a combined listed value of 10,000 GP or less. Components replaced in this way are considered consumed.

entries.name: Unbroken Rite
entries: If a ritual performed with this coin is interrupted, its progress remains intact for 1 hour. If you resume the same ritual during that time, you continue from the point at which it was interrupted rather than beginning again.
The coin can preserve only one unfinished ritual at a time.

race.name: Runeblood
entries: Runeblood are humanoids marked by living arcane inscriptions that form naturally across their bodies.
The markings differ greatly between individuals. Some appear as faint lines beneath the skin, others glow across the eyes or limbs, and some remain invisible until magic is used.
No reliable history explains where the inscriptions originate. Identical symbols have occasionally appeared on Runeblood separated by centuries and with no known relation to one another.

entries.name: Arcane Sight
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.
Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Living Rune
entries: Choose one of the following runes when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Rune.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Force Rune.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d8} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Passage Rune.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Insight Rune.} When you fail an ability check, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success.

entries: You can activate your Living Rune a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Runic Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.

entries.name: Read the Script
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to understand magical runes, glyphs, inscriptions, or written magical effects.

entries.name: Runic Memory
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana} skill. If you already have proficiency in Arcana, you instead gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Inscribed Focus
entries: You can use the runes on your body as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

race.name: Fragmentborn
entries: Fragmentborn are humanoids carrying an unknown fragment within their body, mind, or soul.
A fragment may appear as crystal beneath the skin, an unusual scar, a symbol suspended within an eye, a faint distortion around the body, or nothing visible at all.

Fragments don't appear to share a single origin. Attempts to remove or identify them have produced inconsistent results, and in many cases the fragment seems to exist in a form that can't be physically isolated.

entries.name: Fragment Sense
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot.
Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Nature
entries: Choose one of the following manifestations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Fragment.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Fragment.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Echo Fragment.} When you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
{@b Rift Fragment.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Void Fragment.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.

entries: If your Fragment Nature has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Stability
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter your form against your will.

entries.name: Uncertain Presence
entries: Magic that determines your exact nature, origin, or supernatural identity can reveal that you carry an unusual magical presence, but it doesn't automatically reveal the nature or origin of your fragment.

entries.name: Fragment Resonance
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to identify portals, teleportation effects, magical anomalies, or effects that alter space or reality.

entries.name: Anchored Form
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist being teleported or moved against your will by a magical effect.

race.name: Spellforged
entries: Spellforged are living Constructs built around an internal magical structure known as a Spellcore.
Their bodies vary greatly in material and design. Metal, stone, crystal, porcelain, wood, and stranger substances have all been documented.
No surviving record identifies an original creator, and Spellforged discovered in completely unrelated locations sometimes contain identical internal components.

entries.name: Constructed Existence
entries: You don't need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep.
Magic can't put you to sleep.
You must still complete a Long Rest to gain its benefits. During a Long Rest, you spend at least 6 hours in an inactive state, during which you remain conscious and can see and hear normally.

entries.name: Arcane Chassis
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

entries.name: Integrated Spell Focus
entries: Your body can function as a Spellcasting Focus for any spell you cast that allows the use of a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Arcane Maintenance
entries: When {@spell Mending|XPHB} is cast on you, you can expend one Hit Point Die and roll it. You regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled + your Constitution modifier.
Once you regain Hit Points this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Spellcore Configuration
entries: Choose one of the following configurations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Core.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Core.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Assault Core.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Mobility Core.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Restoration Core.} As a Bonus Action, you or one creature you touch regains {@dice 1d6} + your Proficiency Bonus Hit Points.

entries: If your Spellcore Configuration has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Construct Resilience
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Integrated Compartment
entries: Your body contains a small concealed compartment. It can hold objects with a combined weight of up to 5 pounds, provided each object can fit within a space roughly 1 foot on a side.
Finding the compartment while it is closed requires a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier.
Opening or closing the compartment requires the Utilize action.

race.name: Arcane Aberrant
entries: Arcane Aberrants are humanoids whose bodies have been permanently altered by magical forces.

The changes vary enormously between individuals. One may possess unusually colored blood, crystalline growths beneath the skin, shifting patterns across the eyes, or faint magical distortions surrounding their body. Others appear almost entirely ordinary until their magic begins to surface.

Whether these alterations are inherited, caused by exposure to powerful magic, or originate from something far older remains uncertain. What is known is that the magic within an Arcane Aberrant never remains completely still. Their bodies continue to adapt around it throughout their lives.

entries.name: Age
entries: Arcane Aberrants reach adulthood at roughly the same rate as Humans. Their maximum lifespan is unknown, and no Arcane Aberrant has yet been confirmed to die from old age.

entries.name: Natural Inclination
entries: Increase your Ability Scores by a total of {@b 2 points}.
These increases are separate from those granted by your Background.

entries.name: Gradual Development
entries: When you select this species, choose one Ability Score as your {@b Primary Ability} and a different Ability Score as your {@b Secondary Ability}. These choices are permanent.
At character levels {@b 5, 9, 13, and 17}, your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1}.
Your Secondary Ability further strengthens your Primary Ability. For every {@b 2 points} your Secondary Ability has above 10, your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1}.
If your Secondary Ability increases or decreases enough to cross one of these thresholds, the increase granted to your Primary Ability changes accordingly.
Increases granted by this trait are separate from Ability Score increases granted by your Background, Feats, or other features.

entries.name: Mutative Instinct
entries: When you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
The die becomes {@dice 1d6} when your Proficiency Bonus becomes +4, {@dice 1d8} when it becomes +5, and {@dice 1d10} when it becomes +6.

entries.name: Aberrant Magic
entries: Magic has become an intrinsic part of your body.
You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip.
Starting at character level 3, you can cast {@spell Chromatic Orb|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot or providing its Material component.
Starting at character level 5, you can cast {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot.
You regain the ability to cast each of these spells with this trait when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for these spells.
Your body can serve as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

entries.name: Resilient Metabolism
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Heightened Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill.
You also have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

feat.name: Spell Thief
entries: You have learned to seize the lingering structure of another creature's magic before it fades.

entries.name: Steal Spell
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 or higher, you can take a Reaction to attempt to steal an echo of that spell.
The spell must be of a level no higher than your Proficiency Bonus and no higher than 5th level.
Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, you store the spell within yourself.
You can have only one stolen spell at a time. Stealing another spell causes the previous one to be lost.

entries.name: Stolen Casting
entries: While you have a stolen spell, you can cast it once without expending a spell slot, using the same level at which you stole it.
The stolen spell counts as one of your spells while you hold it, and you use your own spellcasting ability for its attack rolls and saving throw DC.
You must provide any Material components the spell normally requires, including components that have a cost or are consumed.
After you cast the stolen spell, it disappears from you.
If unused, the stolen spell disappears when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Larceny
entries: Once you successfully steal a spell, you can't successfully steal another spell until you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: You have developed an instinctive response to creatures using magic around you.

entries.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to move up to half your Speed.
Immediately after this movement, you can do one of the following against that creature:

items: Make one attack with a weapon.
Cast a cantrip that has a casting time of an Action and makes an attack roll.

entries: This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Spell Resistance
entries: When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you take no damage and suffer no other effect from that spell that would normally occur on a successful save.

feat.name: Spellcrafting
entries: You have learned to dismantle and reconstruct the structure of spells.

entries.name: Spellcrafting
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can choose a different spell you know or have prepared and expend a spell slot capable of casting that spell as well.
Choose any number of the following properties from the second spell and replace the corresponding properties of the spell you are casting:

items: {@b Range.}
{@b Duration.}
{@b Damage Dice and Damage Type.}
{@b Saving Throw.}
{@b Spell Attack.}
{@b Area of Effect.}
{@b Spell Effect.}

entries: You can replace one, several, or all of these properties.
Any part you don't replace remains unchanged from the original spell.

entries.name: Spellcrafting Uses
entries: You can use Spellcrafting a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier, with a minimum of once.
You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
